page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv8 Graviton2 architecture. The instance provides 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) based on the Neoverse-N1 design clocked at 2.5 GHz, without hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB, adhering to a standard 1:2 compute-optimized ratio. Networking provides a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached EBS volumes for persistent storage.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the single-core profile of the instance. In stress-ng single-core tests, the CPU achieves a mid-tier score of 1492.69, which matches its multi-core result due to the single-thread allocation. In Geekbench, the server scores 924.0 in both single-core and multi-core suites, reflecting minimal overall parallel capacity compared to larger multi-core nodes. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 19.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaches 9.74 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates 1.16 million Redis SET operations per second and static web throughput of 1.1 GB/sec.

The c6gn.medium offers cost-effective access to dedicated ARM64 compute resources without noisy-neighbor contention from shared cores. While total compute throughput is strictly bounded by the single core and 2.0 GB memory limit, it provides predictable processing for continuous execution. The server fits ARM application testing, lightweight container hosting, reverse proxying, CI/CD build tasks, and low-volume background microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.medium is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual server powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 core. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 1 vCPU, 2.0 GB of memory, and 2 Gbps baseline networking, without local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance records a stress-ng single-core score of 1492.69 and achieves 1.16 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 1.1 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Overall multi-threaded metrics rank lower across broader hardware distributions due to the physical constraint of a single CPU core. By providing isolated CPU cycles without hyperthreading, c6gn.medium serves as a reliable, resource-efficient platform for running lightweight microservices, network proxies, small web applications, and ARM-native software validation.
